PLANES.rule: Three planes, distinguished because their credentials, their failure modes and their mutation risks are different. A control derived for one plane does not transfer to another.

planes.name: VERCEL CONTROL PLANE
planes.surface: api.vercel.com REST over HTTPS, and/or the vercel CLI measured present at 54.14.2.
planes.credential_class: A Vercel access token, personal or team-scoped.
planes.primary_hazard: The same credential that reads a project setting can change it. The only separation is the HTTP verb and the endpoint chosen, both of which are the acting lane's own discipline. RC-1 and RC-10 exist because there is no platform-enforced read-only mode to lean on.
planes.second_hazard: Some CLI paths write local state into the worktree (a .vercel directory). DN-1's own cost_bound field declares that a path requiring local state is a DIFFERENT act with a different prestate and that the node fails closed rather than performing it. RC-4 carries this.

planes.name: GITHUB SETTINGS PLANE
planes.surface: api.github.com REST over HTTPS, and/or gh api measured present at 2.93.0.
planes.credential_class: A GitHub token with repository administration read scope. Reading branch protection and rulesets requires admin-level access on most configurations, which is a materially more privileged credential than a code-read token.
planes.primary_hazard: The credential required to READ protection is the credential that can DELETE protection. There is no lower-privilege read path for this data, which is why RC-9 requires the scope to be recorded and why G-R2's prohibited_operations list is explicit rather than implied.
planes.second_hazard: Protection lives in TWO namespaces (classic branch protection and repository rulesets) plus a possible organization-level ruleset. A read of one namespace answering 404 proves nothing about the others. DF-3 governs.

planes.name: GIT REF PLANE
planes.surface: git ls-remote against origin. Non-mutating by construction: it has no write mode.
planes.credential_class: Whatever credential the repository requires for a remote listing; for a public repository this may be none.
planes.primary_hazard: NOT mutation. The hazard is a FALSE ABSENCE: a pattern-scoped listing that returns nothing is indistinguishable from a pattern typo or a scoping error. DF-5 and RC-3 govern.

A confirmation prompt is not an intervening act; any mutation, any other lane's act, and any human-scale delay that the acting lane cannot bound IS.
classes.applies_when: The read is the prestate of a mutation, or is a precondition whose falsification would change whether the mutation is safe.
classes.what_it_forbids: Taking the read at the head of a session and citing it at the end of the session.

classes.definition: The read is valid for the duration of ONE measurement lane that performs no mutation on either plane, solely for the purpose of producing a measurement record. It expires at the lane boundary.
classes.applies_when: The read produces evidence for an owner decision or a readiness finding, and no mutation is performed in the same lane.
classes.what_it_forbids: Carrying the value into a later execution lane. A later lane re-reads under F-IMMEDIATE.

A recorded measurement is admissible only as (a) evidence of the instant it names, or (b) a FALSIFICATION TARGET for a fresh measurement.

PRODUCTION_IDENTITY_RULE.statement: PRODUCTION IDENTITY MUST BE MEASURED AND MUST NEVER BE INFERRED FROM A PROJECT NAME, IN EITHER DIRECTION.
the_two_directions: A project whose name contains 'production' (uellix-production-web) MUST NOT be treated as a production surface on that basis. A name is a label a human typed once.

A project whose name does NOT contain 'production' (uellix-antigravity) MUST NOT be treated as non-production on that basis. The chain has already measured that uellix-antigravity IS the project serving www.uellix.com, which is the exact case where the name-based heuristic gives the wrong answer.

what_DOES_constitute_measured_production.rule: A project holds a Commercial V1 PRODUCTION role only on a CONJUNCTION of measured facts, each from an allowlisted field of an authorized read. Any single limb alone is insufficient.
limbs: PIR-a: the project's Git link resolves to lorenzozanello/uellix-antigravity (V-R1 / V-R2 link.repo), OR the project holds some other measured Commercial V1 binding per DN-2's eight limbs.
PIR-b: the project has at least one deployment with target=production (V-R4 / V-R2 deployments limb), with the pagination cursor checked per RC-2.
PIR-c: a custom domain or alias resolves to that project or to one of its deployments (V-R4 alias limb / V-R2 domains limb).

PIR-d: the project's productionBranch and automatic-deployment posture determine whether a future push reaches PIR-b, which is what DN-1 measures and what distinguishes 'has served production' from 'will serve production'.
what_DOES_constitute_measured_production.the_distinction_that_must_not_collapse: PIR-b and PIR-c are statements about what HAS happened and what is CURRENTLY bound. PIR-d is a statement about what WILL happen on the next push. DN-1's MIN-1_scope_bound already refuses a deployment-derived answer as a substitute for the setting; PIR-1 restates it as an identity rule so the same substitution cannot re-enter through DN-2 or DN-11.

PRODUCTION_IDENTITY_RULE.the_asymmetry_for_DN-2: DN-2's predicate is ANY Commercial V1 ROLE, which is strictly broader than a production role. A project can hold a Commercial V1 role while satisfying none of PIR-b, PIR-c or PIR-d: by holding Commercial V1 environment rows, by being bound to a Commercial V1 backing service, or by being dormant with a configuration that would make it a Commercial V1 surface the moment a domain were attached. PIR-1 therefore constrains how a POSITIVE production finding is established; it does NOT narrow DN-2's predicate, and a lane that evaluates only PIR-a..PIR-d has performed a PARTIAL DN-2.

SECRET_BEARING_FIELD_PROHIBITIONS.rule: ABSOLUTE AND NON-WAIVABLE. These fields must not be requested, must not be read, must not be logged, must not be written into any evidence record, any commit, any transcript, any scratch file or any tool output. A response that returns one anyway must be projected to the field allowlist BEFORE anything is persisted, and the occurrence recorded as an incident under RC-6.
SECRET_BEARING_FIELD_PROHIBITIONS.why_stated_as_a_list_rather_than_as_a_pr: A principle ('do not read secrets') is evaluated by the acting lane at the moment it is most inconvenient. An enumerated list is checkable by a certifier and by a harness. Silence in the list is NOT permission; RC-5 makes the allowlist, not this list, the operative control.

PLANE_V_prohibited.field_or_operation: Any environment variable VALUE, and any use of the decrypt=true query parameter on any env endpoint.
PLANE_V_prohibited.why: The value IS the credential. CM-7's own precedent read key, target, gitBranch, type and timestamps only, explicitly via decrypt=false, and explicitly never values. That precedent is carried here as a hard prohibition rather than as a habit.
PLANE_V_prohibited.note: Enumerating rows by NAME and TARGET proves the ABSENCE of a binding by name; it never proves a PRESENT row is innocuous, because the target lives in the value. That limitation is a MEASUREMENT limit to be recorded, never a reason to decrypt.

PLANE_V_prohibited.field_or_operation: The URL of any deploy hook (the url field of any deploy-hook object).
PLANE_V_prohibited.why: A deploy hook URL is a bearer capability: possession of the string is sufficient to trigger a deployment, with no further authentication. Writing one into a docs artifact would create a DURABLE, COMMITTED, PUBLICLY VISIBLE production-mutation capability inside the very repository whose visibility OD-2 ratifies as PUBLIC. The deploy-hook limb of DN-1 is satisfied by the hook's existence, id, name and target ref; it never requires the URL.
PLANE_V_prohibited.allowlisted_substitute: deploy hook id, name, ref, createdAt, and the COUNT with the pagination cursor state.

PLANE_V_prohibited.field_or_operation: Any protection-bypass secret, automation bypass token, or password-protection password on a project (including any field of a passwordProtection object beyond its presence or absence, and any protection-bypass token object beyond its count).
PLANE_V_prohibited.why: These are credentials that defeat the very Deployment Protection posture CM-9 measured. Reading one is acquiring the bypass.

PLANE_V_prohibited.field_or_operation: Any Vercel access token, integration token, OAuth credential, or the response of any endpoint whose purpose is to issue or list tokens.
PLANE_V_prohibited.why: Out of every node's need and squarely in the class of acquiring credentials rather than measuring configuration.

PLANE_V_prohibited.field_or_operation: Any git credential material behind the Git integration, including any credential id resolved to its secret, and any webhook signing secret.
PLANE_V_prohibited.why: A credential id is an opaque handle and is allowlisted where a node needs it; the credential itself never is.

PLANE_V_prohibited.field_or_operation: Deployment build logs, runtime logs, and function logs on any deployment.
PLANE_V_prohibited.why: No node requires them, and they are the least predictable container of incidental secret material on the platform. Excluded by the allowlist and named here so 'just to see why' does not become a path.

PLANE_G_prohibited.field_or_operation: Any GitHub Actions secret, Dependabot secret, Codespaces secret, or environment secret, in any form, and any Actions VARIABLE value.
PLANE_G_prohibited.why: No node of this DAG requires them. The eight required-check names are job names in tracked workflow files, not secrets.

PLANE_G_prohibited.field_or_operation: The raw exposed credential of any secret-scanning alert (the secret field of an alert object), and any alert LOCATION payload that embeds it.
PLANE_G_prohibited.why: DN-17 is not authorized here at all, but the alert endpoints sit on the same host as G-R1..G-R3 and the same token may reach them. Reading an alert's raw secret would re-expose, into a new artifact, exactly the credential PR #206's lane exists to adjudicate. Stated so proximity does not become permission.

PLANE_G_prohibited.field_or_operation: Any webhook configuration secret (the config.secret of a repository or organization webhook), any deploy key (public or private), and any GitHub App installation token.
PLANE_G_prohibited.why: Out of every node's need; each is a credential rather than a configuration fact.

PLANE_G_prohibited.field_or_operation: The GitHub token used to perform the reads, in any evidence record, any log, any error message and any commit.
PLANE_G_prohibited.why: A token echoed into a redacted-by-hand error string is the commonest way a credential reaches a public repository. RC-6 requires redaction BEFORE persistence, not after review.

PLANE_X_prohibited.field_or_operation: Any credential embedded in a remote URL, and any remote URL variant carrying a token (a https://<token>@github.com/... form).
PLANE_X_prohibited.why: X-R1 targets origin as configured. If the configured remote were ever to carry an embedded credential, the evidence record must name the remote by its canonical credential-free form and record that a credential-bearing form was observed, without reproducing it.

PLANE_X_prohibited.field_or_operation: Any object content. X-R1 lists refs and SHAs only; it does not fetch, and it does not read blobs or commit bodies from the remote.
PLANE_X_prohibited.why: A ref listing is the minimum that answers the prestate question. Fetching is a larger act with a different failure surface and is not required by any limb.

READS.rule: NINE reads. Each declares, per the directing mission's contract: exact endpoint or tool surface, field allowlist, secret-bearing fields prohibited, freshness, target identity, evidence record and failure token. A read not listed here is not authorized, and a field not allowlisted is not authorized even on a listed read.

pinning_convention.PINNED: The operation is cited to a CORRECTED_MEASUREMENTS entry of CV1_INFRA_RELEASE_CONTROL_AUTHORITY_AMENDMENT_v1.0.1.json, which records a prior lane actually performing it. A PINNED operation is evidenced to have existed at that measurement's date. It is NOT evidenced to be current: DN-1's MIN-1 states that an endpoint versioned away is an infrastructure failure of the measurement, not evidence about the setting. RC-7 carries that as a general rule.
pinning_convention.RECALLED_NOT_PINNED: No artifact in the chain records this operation being performed. The endpoint path and field names are RECALLED and are therefore UNVERIFIED. A RECALLED operation MUST be resolved against the provider's live API surface at read time before it is relied upon, and a field that does not appear under its recalled name MUST NOT be reported as an absent FEATURE. RC-8 governs.
pinning_convention.why_this_distinction_is_load_bearing: The Vercel plane has one lane of endpoint precedent behind it; the GitHub settings plane has NONE, because UD-2 records that no lane in this chain has ever performed an authenticated GitHub settings read. Presenting both with equal confidence would manufacture evidence for the weaker half.

If no allowlisted field carries the semantic content, the read is INCOMPLETE and DN-1 DOES NOT DISCHARGE.
the_automatic_deployment_limb.what_the_incomplete_result_does_NOT_lice: It does not license proceeding on the assumption that automatic deployment is enabled, nor on the assumption that it is disabled. DN-1's own third fail-closed branch already states that a disabled toggle relaxes no control. An UNEXPOSED toggle relaxes even less.
the_automatic_deployment_limb.why_this_is_written_as_a_gap_rather_than: Naming a plausible field here would convert a recalled string into an authority-blessed one, and a subsequent lane finding that field absent would conclude the FEATURE was absent. RC-8 exists for exactly this, and the honest posture is to state the semantic requirement and let the read fail closed if the platform does not expose it.

The SAME read re-executed as the precondition of M-7 or M-6 is a prestate, and a prestate taken at the head of a session and cited at the end of it is not a prestate. the_declared_insufficiency.why_this_is_stated_rather_than_hoped: An authority that grants a read and lets the consumer discover the insufficiency at execution time has moved a known blocker downstream. the_declared_insufficiency.what_would_close_it: Either a Vercel surface that exposes per-branch automatic-deployment toggles read-only, discovered and pinned by the acting lane; or an owner-side reading of the project's Git settings in the dashboard, which is the second admissible path U-1's resolved_by field already names and which this artifact does not and cannot constrain.

reads.name: REF_PROTECTION_STATE_ACROSS_BOTH_NAMESPACES

the_two_namespaces_finding.statement: O-1 requires 'branch protection OR a repository ruleset'. These are TWO SEPARATE NAMESPACES on GitHub with separate endpoints, separate data shapes and separate precedence. A read of one returning 404 establishes nothing about the other.
the_two_namespaces_finding.why_this_is_load_bearing_here: The parent records main's protection as 'Measured ABSENT (404) at the parent's authoring'. A 404 from the classic branch-protection endpoint is consistent with a repository ruleset fully protecting the branch. A lane re-measuring DN-8 with a single endpoint and getting 404 would report 'unprotected', configure classic protection, and have measured neither the prestate nor the result.
the_two_namespaces_finding.the_rule: EVERY per-ref protection measurement MUST read BOTH namespaces AND the effective-rules view, and MUST report the UNION. A finding of 'unprotected' requires all three to agree.

limb_A_classic_branch_protection.note: A 404 here means NO CLASSIC PROTECTION, and nothing more. It MUST be recorded with that exact scope.

limb_B_repository_rulesets.operation: GET https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/rulesets (paginated), then GET .../rulesets/{id} for each, to obtain its conditions and rules.
limb_B_repository_rulesets.note: The LIST form typically omits the rules and conditions. Reading only the list and concluding what a ruleset enforces is a shape error, not a scoping error. Each ruleset MUST be fetched individually.

limb_C_effective_rules_for_a_ref.purpose: Returns the rules ACTUALLY APPLYING to that branch, including rules inherited from organization-level rulesets that limb B may not enumerate. This is the closest thing to a single authoritative answer and is therefore REQUIRED, not optional.
limb_C_effective_rules_for_a_ref.the_org_caveat: If the repository sits under an organization, an org-level ruleset may be invisible to limb B and may not be fully attributable in limb C. If the effective view shows a rule limb B cannot account for, the source is UNKNOWN and is recorded as such. STOP_RULESET_SOURCE_UNATTRIBUTABLE.

limb_D_pattern_match_for_a_nonexistent_r.operation: Limb B's ruleset inventory, with each ruleset's conditions.ref_name include and exclude PATTERNS inspected locally.
limb_D_pattern_match_for_a_nonexistent_r.why_it_is_a_separate_limb: DN-7's prestate asks whether any protection or ruleset ALREADY MATCHES release/**. release/commercial-v1 DOES NOT EXIST at that moment, so limbs A and C cannot be evaluated against it: a per-branch endpoint for a nonexistent branch returns 404 and that 404 is about the BRANCH, not about the RULES. The question is answerable ONLY by inspecting ruleset PATTERNS. See DF-4.

the ~ALL and ~DEFAULT_BRANCH special refs, which match without naming a pattern at all

A lane whose tooling templates a method is one character from deleting the protection it came to measure. RC-1 requires the verb be stated explicitly on every invocation, and this is the read that motivates it.

the_careful_scoping_of_this_read.minimality_note: This read SURVIVED the minimality test only in this falsification role. CROSS_CUTTING_READ_CONTROLS.rule: These bind EVERY read. A read's own block may tighten them and may never relax them.

controls.name: EXPLICIT VERB
controls.control: Every HTTP operation states its method explicitly, and every gh api invocation carries --method GET explicitly. No operation relies on a tool's default verb.
controls.why: gh api defaults to GET but is silently promoted to POST when a body is present, and the branch-protection GET, PUT and DELETE forms share one path. The separation between reading protection and destroying it is one word on the command line.

controls.name: PAGINATION EXHAUSTION BEFORE ANY COUNT OR ABSENCE CLAIM
controls.control: Every listing follows its cursor or Link header to exhaustion, and records the TERMINAL state. No count, no first row and no absence claim may be made from a page.
controls.why: CM-3 records this programme producing a wrong figure twice from a default page size, and generalizes: any successor citing a platform listing MUST check the pagination cursor before treating a count or a first row as complete.

controls.name: AN EMPTY TOOL RESULT IS NOT AN ABSENCE IN THE WORLD
controls.control: An empty or negative result from ONE surface is recorded as a fact about that surface. A claim of absence requires either a second surface agreeing, or an explicit statement that the claim is scoped to the surface read.
controls.why: CM-4 records an empty CLI alias table being read as an absence of aliases, when the API returned them. The parent's own lesson: the emptiness was an artefact of the CLI surface, not a fact about the aliases; re-measurement discipline is needed across TOOLS, not only across TIME.

controls.name: NO LOCAL STATE WRITTEN BY A READ
controls.control: No authorized read may write state into the worktree, including any link or pull step that creates a project-link directory or an environment file. If the only available path to a field requires writing local state, the read FAILS CLOSED and the node does not discharge.
controls.why: DN-1's cost_bound states this in terms: a path requiring local state is a DIFFERENT act with a different prestate, and the node fails closed rather than performing it. It also protects the scope gate: an unexpected untracked directory collapses to a single git status line unless --untracked-files=all is passed.

controls.name: THE ALLOWLIST IS THE GRANT
controls.control: A field not named in a read's field_allowlist is not authorized, whether or not it appears in SECRET_BEARING_FIELD_PROHIBITIONS. Silence in the prohibition list is not permission; the allowlist is positive and the prohibition list is an emphasis on its most dangerous exclusions.
controls.why: A prohibition list can never be exhaustive of a provider's evolving response shape. An allowlist can be exhaustive of a node's need.

controls.name: REDACT BEFORE PERSIST
controls.control: A response is projected to the allowlist BEFORE anything is written to disk, to a transcript, to a log or to a commit. Raw bodies are never persisted. If a prohibited field is returned anyway, the occurrence is recorded as an incident naming the field, and the value is never reproduced.
controls.conditioned_by: G-R1's visibility read: the repository is measured PUBLIC under OD-2, so anything committed is world-readable immediately and irrevocably. jq is ABSENT on this machine (RP-3), so the obligation cannot be delegated to a filter that is not installed.

controls.name: ENDPOINT VERSION DRIFT IS AN INFRASTRUCTURE FAILURE, NOT EVIDENCE
controls.control: Each read records the API version segment it issued. If a PINNED operation returns 404 or 410, or omits an allowlisted field it is pinned to have returned, the result is an INFRASTRUCTURE FAILURE OF THE MEASUREMENT and the node does not discharge. It is never evidence about the setting.
controls.why: DN-1's MIN-1 states it directly: the citation establishes that a read-only path existed and what it was, but does NOT establish that the same endpoint version is still current, so DN-1 must re-verify the OPERATION as well as the VALUE.

controls.name: A RECALLED OPERATION IS RESOLVED BEFORE IT IS RELIED UPON
controls.control: An operation marked RECALLED_NOT_PINNED must be resolved against the provider's live API surface at read time, and the resolved form recorded. A field that does not appear under its recalled name MUST NOT be reported as an absent FEATURE; it is an UNRESOLVED FIELD NAME until the live surface says otherwise.
controls.why: The whole GitHub limb is RECALLED, because UD-2 records that no lane in this chain has ever performed an authenticated GitHub settings read. Treating a recalled field name's absence as a feature's absence would manufacture a negative finding out of a memory.

controls.name: CREDENTIAL PROVENANCE AND SCOPE RECORDED BEFORE THE FIRST READ
controls.control: Before the first read of a lane, the acting lane records, for each plane: where the credential came from, what scope or permission it carries, and what it could mutate if misused. For PLANE-G it additionally records the authenticated permission object returned by G-R1.
controls.why: Reading branch protection generally requires an admin-level credential, which is the credential that can DELETE protection. The elevated privilege is a property of the READ that must be visible to a certifier, not a detail of how the read happened to be performed.

controls.name: NO SCOPE CREEP FROM A CREDENTIAL IN HAND
controls.control: Holding a credential that CAN perform an operation is not authorization to perform it. Any operation not enumerated in READS is refused, recorded, and escalated as an authority question rather than performed and disclosed afterwards.
controls.why: Both planes' credentials are far broader than this grant. The grant attaches to the reads, not to the reader.

controls.name: SCOPE AMBIGUITY IS NOT ABSENCE
controls.control: On PLANE-V, a 404 from a scope-qualified or scope-unqualified request is recorded as a fact about THAT SCOPE. A project is ABSENT only when every enumerated scope returns 404 and the scope enumeration itself is recorded exhaustive. On PLANE-G, a 404 may equally mean 'not visible to this credential'.
controls.why: DN-2's predicate is an absence claim, and an absence claim from one scope is the commonest way to under-measure an account.

controls.name: ABSENT FROM THE RESPONSE IS DISTINGUISHED FROM PRESENT AND NULL
controls.control: For every allowlisted field not carrying a value, the record states whether the KEY was absent from the response or PRESENT with a null or empty value. Where the two cannot be distinguished, the field is UNRESOLVED, not absent.
controls.why: CM-8 concludes 'commandForIgnoringBuildStep is ABSENT (no Ignored Build Step is configured)'. That inference is sound only if the provider omits the key when unset rather than returning it null, and the distinction is unrecorded. DN-14's rollback depends on which is true, because restoring 'absent' and restoring 'null' are different operations.

controls.name: NO READ IS A NODE'S DISCHARGE
controls.control: Performing a read authorized here satisfies a node's MEASUREMENT obligation only. It never satisfies the node's verification clause, never satisfies its confirmation requirement, and never authorizes the mutation the node names. DN-1 discharged does not authorize DN-8.
controls.why: This artifact's authority_class is READ_ONLY_CONTROL_PLANE_MEASUREMENT_AUTHORITY__NOT_AN_EXECUTION_AUTHORITY, and the parent's adjudication Q states there is no control-plane mutation a successor may perform on standing authority.

controls.name: A PARTIAL MEASUREMENT IS RECORDED AS PARTIAL AND LEAVES ITS STOP ARMED
controls.control: Where a read evaluates fewer than all the limbs its node enumerates, the finding is PARTIAL, the unevaluated limbs remain UNKNOWN, and any STOP attached to them remains armed. A PARTIAL finding is never reported as a clean result.
controls.why: DN-2's third fail-closed branch states it exactly: partial absence is not absence. V-R2's L6 forces a PARTIAL by construction, and V-R3 is known in advance to be likely PARTIAL per CM-8.

DERIVED_FINDINGS.rule: Findings this lane derived while converting nodes into reads. Each changes what a read must do. None is a restatement of a source clause.

findings.finding: ONE OF THE EIGHT REQUIRED CHECK NAMES CONTAINS COMMAS.
findings.measured: ADJUDICATIONS.D.required_checks is an array of EIGHT strings whose first entry is 'Lint, typecheck, test, build'. That exact string is the job-level name at .github/workflows/ci.yml:11, measured at the parent HEAD.
findings.the_hazard: A lane, script or harness that flattens or comma-splits the required-check list sees ELEVEN names where there are EIGHT, and then finds four of them ('Lint', 'typecheck', 'test', 'build') unproducible by any workflow. It would report a rider violation that does not exist, or, configuring from the same split list, would require four check contexts nothing can ever produce, creating exactly the permanently unsatisfiable gate RIDER_PRE_1 exists to prevent.
findings.the_control: G-R2 limb E and G-R4 both require comparison by WHOLE-STRING EQUALITY over the entire name, with the comparison method stated in the evidence record. Splitting any required-check name on any delimiter is prohibited.
findings.why_it_survived_this_far: The list reads as prose. Eight entries where one entry looks like four is invisible to a human scan and to any check that only counts.

findings.finding: A NAME-KEY SWEEP OVER THE WORKFLOW CORPUS OVER-COUNTS JOB NAMES.
findings.measured: golden-journey.yml line 162 carries a step-level artifact name value. The eight required checks are JOB-level names. A sweep matching every name key in the corpus returns both.
findings.the_hazard: The PRODUCIBLE predicate is defined over 'a job whose name value equals c exactly'. A parse matching name keys at any nesting depth can match a step-level or artifact-level name and report a check producible that no job produces.
findings.the_control: The corpus parse underlying DN-4 must match name at JOB level specifically, and the evidence record must state the nesting level matched. This is a control on the tracked-file parse, which needs no authority; it is recorded here because G-R4 is the read that would falsify it.

findings.finding: A 404 FROM THE CLASSIC BRANCH-PROTECTION ENDPOINT IS NOT ABSENCE OF PROTECTION.
findings.derivation: O-1 requires 'branch protection OR a repository ruleset'. These are two namespaces with separate endpoints. The parent records main's protection as measured ABSENT (404) at its authoring. If that 404 came from the classic endpoint alone, it is consistent with a ruleset protecting main completely.
findings.the_hazard: DN-8, DN-9, DN-10 and DN-12 each re-measure protection. A lane reading one namespace, getting 404, and reporting 'unprotected' would (a) mis-state the prestate, (b) configure classic protection redundantly or conflictingly with an existing ruleset, and (c) report O-1 satisfied on evidence that never examined half of what O-1 names.
findings.the_control: G-R2's three-limb requirement and its STOP_PROTECTION_NAMESPACE_INCOMPLETE. A verdict of NOT PROTECTED requires all three limbs read and agreeing.
findings.relation_to_prior_art: This is the same shape as the programme's measured lesson that an enumeration proves absence only over what it enumerated, applied to a namespace split rather than to a row set.

findings.finding: THE PRE-CREATION PROTECTION QUESTION FOR THE RELEASE BRANCH CANNOT BE ANSWERED BY A PER-BRANCH READ.
findings.derivation: M-8's prestate asks whether any branch protection or ruleset ALREADY MATCHES the pattern release/** on this repository, because such a ruleset would apply to the ref THE INSTANT IT IS CREATED and would change what M-9 has to do. At that moment release/commercial-v1 does not exist, so every per-branch endpoint returns 404 ABOUT THE BRANCH.
findings.the_hazard: A lane asking 'is release/commercial-v1 protected?' via a per-branch endpoint receives 404, records 'not protected', creates the branch under M-8's REQUIRED (not ELEVATED) confirmation, and discovers a ruleset was matching it all along. M-8's own escalation clause, which raises its confirmation to ELEVATED exactly when this limb is dirty, would never have fired.
findings.the_control: G-R2 limb D is a RULESET PATTERN inspection, structurally different from limbs A and C, with an enumerated list of pattern forms that must each be evaluated and recorded, including the special refs that match without naming a pattern. TI-19 additionally requires the record to state that the ref does not exist, so the 404s are not later misread.

findings.finding: A PATTERN-SCOPED LS-REMOTE CANNOT DISTINGUISH ABSENCE FROM A TYPO.
findings.derivation: M-8's prestate requires the COMPLETE ABSENCE of refs/heads/release/* and refs/tags/release/*. The natural command carries the pattern as a refspec. Empty output then has at least four causes: the refs are genuinely absent; the pattern was misspelled; the shell expanded or consumed the glob; or the remote resolved to something unexpected. All four look identical.
findings.the_hazard: The absence claim is a PRESTATE for a mutation. A false absence permits M-8 to create a ref over a ref that already exists, or to proceed believing a clean prestate it never measured.
findings.the_control: X-R1 mandates the UNFILTERED form with local filtering, mandates recording the TOTAL ref count as a non-emptiness witness, and mandates the two limbs be reported separately rather than aggregated. A zero total is a failed read, not an empty remote.
findings.the_second_limb_it_also_protects: An invocation carrying --heads silently drops the refs/tags/release/* limb the prestate names. The unfiltered form carries both.

findings.finding: DN-12'S READ ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING AND WAS CARRIED ONLY IMPLICITLY.
findings.derivation: DN-12's target is 'the repository default branch', identified by ROLE. Its re_measurement_required names both WHICH branch is the default and that branch's protection endpoints. The second read's TARGET is the first read's OUTPUT.
findings.the_hazard: A lane performing the protection read against an assumed target (feature/sprint-0-foundation, which the parent names as the thing not to assume) and the default-branch read afterwards as a confirmation would have protected a branch chosen from memory and then confirmed the memory. The two reads would both pass.
findings.the_control: G-R3 MUST precede G-R2 for DN-12, TI-18 requires G-R2's evidence record to carry G-R3's output and timestamp as its target's provenance, and TI-20 makes the measured name the only admissible target. A later G-R3 returning a different name is STOP_DEFAULT_BRANCH_CHANGED_MID_LANE, not a value to choose between.

findings.finding: DN-2'S ABSENCE CLAIM IS SCOPE-RELATIVE AND THE SCOPE SET WAS NEVER ENUMERATED.
findings.derivation: DN-2's predicate ranges over 'every other project in the account'. On Vercel, projects live in a personal scope and in zero or more team scopes, each addressed by a separate qualifier. A project listing without an enumerated scope set is a listing of one scope.
findings.the_hazard: The reported narrow finding U6_RESOLVED_NO_SECOND_ACTIVE_PROJECT rests on uellix-antigravity being the sole active project serving current Commercial V1 custom domains. If that was measured in one scope, a second scope holding uellix-production-web would be invisible, and the broad re-measurement DN-2 exists to perform would reproduce the same blind spot under a broader vocabulary. A sweep by vocabulary catches what it was told to look for; it does not widen the surface it swept.
findings.the_control: V-R2 step 1 makes SCOPE ENUMERATION the first operation, step 3 addresses uellix-production-web BY NAME in every enumerated scope, RC-11 forbids reading any 404 as absence, and TI-8 requires the credential's own visibility limit be recorded so an invisible project is UNKNOWN rather than absent.

findings.finding: EAD-4 UNDER-ENUMERATES ITS OWN PLANES AND ITS OWN NODES.
findings.derivation: EAD-4 names 'DN-1 and DN-2, and DN-3' and describes the missing authority as one permitting 'an authenticated Vercel control-plane read'. Partitioning NODE_TO_READ_MAP by plane gives: GitHub settings SEVEN nodes (DN-4, DN-7, DN-8, DN-9, DN-10, DN-11, DN-12); git ref plane TWO (DN-5, DN-7); and Vercel SIX (DN-1, DN-2, DN-3, DN-7, DN-11, DN-14) rather than the three EAD-4 names. The under-enumeration is therefore of BOTH KINDS: a whole plane omitted, and the named plane's own node set understated.
findings.a_recurrence_of_this_failure_inside_this: This lane's own first draft wrote the GitHub set as FIVE nodes, omitting DN-8 and DN-9, because it was written from prose recall rather than by partitioning the map. It was caught by computing the partition. Recorded because it demonstrates the failure is not a lapse peculiar to the parent: an enumeration written as a sentence drifts from the structure it summarizes, in the same document that identifies the drift. SC-23 makes the partition the operative statement and the prose derivative of it.
findings.why_this_is_not_a_contradiction_of_the_p: The parent DOES record the GitHub need, as UD-2 ('an authenticated GitHub repository-settings read, which this lane did not perform') and UD-4. The finding is that the need is recorded in the UNKNOWNS register and not folded into the EXTERNAL_AUTHORITY_DEPENDENCIES entry that a successor reads to learn what authority is missing. EAD-4's own field says it is 'the first thing the next gate should see' — and what it shows is one plane of three.
findings.the_hazard_it_creates: A lane commissioned to close EAD-4 as written would have obtained a Vercel read authority, declared the gap closed, and discovered at DN-8 that protection is unreadable. The DAG would have stalled at its fourth node with an authority that had just been certified as sufficient.
findings.the_control: This artifact spans three planes. PURPOSE.the_scope_correction_this_lane_measured states the correction, NODE_TO_READ_MAP proves it node by node, and the coverage_check makes the enumeration auditable.
findings.what_this_finding_does_NOT_do: It does not amend EAD-4, does not edit the parent, and does not claim the parent erred. It records that the gap's declared scope is narrower than the gap, and closes the wider one.

findings.finding: CLOSING EAD-4 DOES NOT UNBLOCK DN-3 OR DN-14, AND THAT IS ALREADY MEASURED.
findings.derivation: CM-8 resolves U-5 as PARTIALLY RESOLVED and states that per-branch automatic-deployment toggles were NOT EXPOSED by the endpoints that lane read, and that M-6's mandatory prestate capture is retained because a partial prestate is not a prestate.
findings.the_hazard: A next gate reading 'EAD-4 closed' would reasonably conclude DN-1, DN-2 and DN-3 are now executable and that DN-14 follows. DN-3 is now ATTEMPTABLE; on the evidence available it is expected to return PARTIAL, and a PARTIAL DN-3 blocks DN-14 by DN-3's own fail_closed.
findings.the_control: V-R3's the_declared_insufficiency block states this before any credential is issued, names STOP_U5_PRESTATE_PARTIAL, and names the two things that would actually close it: a read-only surface exposing per-branch toggles, or the owner-side dashboard reading that U-1's resolved_by field already names as the second admissible path.
findings.the_honest_statement: An authority cannot make a platform expose a field. This one authorizes the attempt and refuses to let the attempt's likely failure be discovered downstream.

findings.finding: A DEPLOY HOOK URL IS A COMMITTABLE PRODUCTION-MUTATION CAPABILITY, AND THE DEPLOY-HOOK LIMB IS MANDATORY.
findings.derivation: DN-1's deploy-hook limb is mandatory because a deploy hook is an independent path to a production deployment that does not pass through any branch push and is therefore invisible to the productionBranch setting entirely. The limb requires knowing whether hooks EXIST. The natural read returns the hook objects, and a hook object carries a URL that is a bearer capability.
findings.the_hazard: The evidence record for DN-1 is a committed artifact in a repository OD-2 ratifies as PUBLIC. A deploy-hook URL written into it is a world-readable, durable trigger for a production deployment, published by the very lane whose purpose is to measure the production boundary.
findings.the_control: SBP-V2 prohibits the URL absolutely and names the allowlisted substitute: id, name, ref, createdAt and the COUNT with its pagination state. Those satisfy the limb completely; the limb asks whether a hook exists and what it targets, never how to fire it.
findings.the_second_order_point: DN-11's verification additionally requires asserting that no deploy hook was created or activated by the act. That assertion is made over the allowlisted projection, comparing counts, ids and refs across the pre-act and post-act records. It never requires a URL either.

why_no_head_or_tree_is_pinned_in_this_bl.the_omission_is_deliberate: The HEAD and TREE at which these gates ran are NOT recorded here.
why_no_head_or_tree_is_pinned_in_this_bl.the_reason: This block was added to the artifact AFTER the gates ran, and adding it changes the tree and, on amendment, the commit. Any HEAD or TREE written here would therefore name the commit that this very edit supersedes: a document pinning its own pre-edit state under a gate-passed claim. The programme has measured that exact failure, where an artifact pinned the blob of its own pre-commit draft under a MANDATORY AND VERIFIED heading while every external pin was correct.
why_no_head_or_tree_is_pinned_in_this_bl.what_a_consumer_does_instead: Re-run the gates at the head under review. The gate output above is a record that they passed on this lane's write set, not a certificate bound to a commit id. AS_OF_PARENT_HEAD and AS_OF_PARENT_TREE pin the PARENT, which does not move, and the nine blob pins of EFFECTIVE_PACKAGE_CONSUMED pin external files, which likewise do not move under this lane's own edits. Those are the pins a certifier verifies.
why_no_head_or_tree_is_pinned_in_this_bl.the_general_rule_this_instantiates: An artifact may pin anything outside itself. It may not pin its own materialization state, because the act of recording the pin changes the state being pinned.

MACHINE_GATES_EXECUTED_THIS_LANE.what_these_gates_do_NOT_establish: Nothing about the correctness of the read set. They establish that the write set is in scope, that the sealed corpus is intact, that the tree carries no credential material and that the repository still typechecks. Whether the nine reads are minimum, sufficient and correctly bounded is a semantic question no gate here evaluates, and is what required_independent_review exists for.

required_independent_review.why_it_is_required_before_arming: This artifact's grant is the first in the chain that lets a lane touch either hosted control plane. A defect in a field allowlist, in a freshness class or in a prohibition is a defect that reaches production infrastructure. WHAT_THIS_ARTIFACT_GRANTS_AND_WHEN records ARMED = FALSE for that reason.
the_reviewer_must_independently: Re-derive all nine blob pins of EFFECTIVE_PACKAGE_CONSUMED from the head under review, and treat any mismatch as STOP_READ_AUTHORITY_BINDING_MISMATCH rather than as an editorial slip.

Perform its OWN node-by-node pass over all 18 nodes of the effective DAG and independently compute the read set, then compare it to READS. A reviewer that only checks the map for internal consistency has checked the map, not the derivation. DF-8 exists because the declared gap and the derived gap differed.
Attempt the MINIMALITY test independently: strike each read in turn and identify the node clause that becomes unsatisfiable. SC-20 records this as unproven here.
Check every PINNED claim against the cited CORRECTED_MEASUREMENTS entry by reading it, not by trusting the citation.
Check that no field allowlist admits a value the SECRET_BEARING_FIELD_PROHIBITIONS forbid, and that RC-5's positive-allowlist framing is not undercut anywhere.
Verify that no read's permitted methods include anything but GET, and that no evidence_record requires persisting a raw response.
Independently evaluate DF-1 by reading ADJUDICATIONS.D.required_checks and counting its array entries, and by reading .github/workflows/ci.yml at the head under review.

Independently evaluate DF-3 and DF-4 against the GitHub protection and ruleset model, and judge whether the three-limb requirement and the pattern limb are sufficient, or whether a fourth limb exists that this derivation missed.
Judge whether RNA-1's boundary is correctly drawn: whether V-R2's L5 grant could be read as covering PMV-2, and whether the target-based distinction holds.
Confirm that this artifact performed no read, by examining its write set and by checking that no value in it about the hosted world is presented as measured by this lane.
what_a_reviewer_should_NOT_treat_as_defe: The GitHub limb being RECALLED_NOT_PINNED. That is UR-2, an honest consequence of UD-2, and pinning it would require performing the forbidden read.
V-R3 being expected to return PARTIAL. That is DF-9, surfaced deliberately rather than discovered downstream.
The absence of a repository-visibility read for DN-16. It was dropped on the minimality test and the reason is recorded.
